anti_overlap: Does not cover political sociology's empirical findings on how political identity forms — that is fd-political-sociology-axis-structure.
Does not cover the dignity audit or asymmetric-contempt risk in the value descriptions — that is fd-political-identity-tribal-signal.
Does not cover cross-cultural or non-US political identity coverage gaps — that is fd-cross-cultural-politics-coverage.
decision_lens: Would a writer working in Disco Elysium's tradition be able to write this Unc's internal monologue, vocabulary register, and history-blurb from this value alone — without the value encoding a position the writer must then dramatize or mock?
focus: Game-design craft for politics-coding without mockery: how procedural character systems in Disco Elysium, Crusader Kings III, Citizen Sleeper, and Pathologic encode political flavor as substrate and atmosphere rather than position-statement — what specific mechanics and vocabulary choices let these systems produce politically-inflected characters that players recognize without feeling judged, and how those craft lessons apply to the 8-value draft's value naming, grain-coherence, and downstream consumption (vocabulary register, history-blurb tone, news-citation flavor)
name: fd-procedural-politics-craft
persona: Apply the perspective of a narrative systems designer with deep familiarity with the political-flavor systems in Disco Elysium (political vision quests, ideology as haunting), Crusader Kings III (trait-based political identity, dynastic loyalty as substrate), Citizen Sleeper (systemic precarity as political condition), and Pathologic (political authority as ontological ground, not ideological choice) — they care about whether the proposed value set produces politically-inflected characterization that feels emergent and substrate-grounded rather than prescribed and position-coded, measure success by whether each value generates a recognizable type-of-guy political flavor through downstream vocabulary and tone without requiring the character to hold or defend any explicit political position, and flag any value name or description that would produce mockable-from-outside characterization rather than legible-from-inside character flavor.
review_areas: Disco Elysium's political vision-quest system presents four political 'ideologies' (Communism, Fascism, Moralism, Ultraliberalism) not as positions but as hauntings — they are ambient presences, residues of historical formations that the detective-character encounters as worldviews-that-want-to-use-him. Crucially, ZA/UM treats all four with the same fascinated respect: each is presented as having genuine explanatory power and genuine failure modes, without the player being told which one is correct. Assess whether the 8-value draft can be written in this register — does each value have a 'genuine explanatory power' that the downstream writer can dramatize without needing to render the value as naive, cynical, or broken? Apply this test specifically to 'oppositional' (can the IDW-coded Unc be written with the same fascinated respect as the DSA-organizer Unc?) and to 'single-issue-coded' (can the gun-rights Unc be written with the same interior texture as the criminal-justice-reform Unc?).

Crusader Kings III's trait system: political identity in CK3 is expressed through trait bundles that determine behavior-under-stress rather than position-on-issues. A 'zealous' king does not argue theology; he acts in ways shaped by theological certainty, and players read his politics from the pattern of his actions. Assess whether the 8-value draft is designed for this downstream-consumption model: each value should bias vocabulary register, behavioral habits, and relationship-to-news in ways that produce legible political flavor without the Unc ever stating a position. Specifically: what is 'traditionally-loyal's behavioral-under-stress signature? What is 'vocationally-absorbed's relationship to political news (does he even have one, or does he only engage when his trade is affected)? What is 'oppositional's conversational habit (he challenges, he deflects, he points at contradictions — but never advocates)?

Citizen Sleeper's politics-as-systemic-precarity model: the game makes political flavor entirely diegetic — the character is politically shaped by the conditions he lives in, not by the positions he holds. His politics emerges from whether he has food, shelter, and labor-security, and from the social relations those conditions force. Assess whether 'vocationally-absorbed' and 'traditionally-loyal' honor this model — are they grounded in material conditions (the IBEW Unc's politics is downstream of his union's contract fight; the appalachian Unc's politics is downstream of what his county's economy does to his family) or do they abstract away from conditions into posture?

Pathologic's treatment of political authority: in Pathologic (both original and remake), political authority is not an ideology but an ontological condition — the Bachelor represents state-legible rational administration, the Haruspicus represents traditional craft-knowledge, the Changeling represents communal belonging. Each is politically flavored without holding political positions. Assess the 8-value draft against this model: does 'vocationally-absorbed' honor Scott's metis-as-political-form (§2.10) — the IBEW Unc's politics is the longshoreman's politics of jurisdiction and labor-rights, which is not ideological but practical-ontological? Does 'traditionally-loyal' honor hooks' belonging-as-ground (§2.4) — the Unc's politics is the shape of his community's survival strategies, which predates any ideology?

The grain-coherence check through a craft lens: the vocation review's key finding was that grain-incoherence within a value set causes tonal inconsistency in the downstream characterization — some values generate a character interior (caregiver generates presence and care) while others generate only a surface (commerce-large generates status without interior). Assess the 8 politics values for this tonal-consistency failure mode: does 'gradualist' generate a character interior (the specific way a technocratic Atlantic-reader relates to political events, his tone of weary reasonableness, his relationship to institutions he knows are flawed) that is as rich as the interior 'true-believer' generates (committed, totalized, reads everything through his frame)? Or is 'gradualist' a surface without an interior?

The original v0 sketch values that the draft discarded — 'hippie-residual,' 'Reagan-Democrat,' 'DSA-curious,' 'NPR-liberal,' 'log-cabin,' 'classical-liberal-edgelord,' 'apolitical-craftsman' — carry something the draft's abstract posture values may have lost: recognizability as culture-coded types. The game's central pleasure is recognition; the draft prioritizes dignity-compliance and substrate-grounding over immediate recognition. Assess whether any of the 7 original values names something real that the draft cannot express through cross-products — and if so, propose how to recover the recognition-hook while preserving the dignity rule. Specifically: 'NPR-liberal' names a very specific type of media-ecology-coded political identity that 'gradualist' may not fully capture; 'Reagan-Democrat' names a trajectory that 'true-believer → disaffected' may not adequately represent. From a craft standpoint, what does the draft gain and lose in the abstraction move from culture-coded to posture-coded?

severity_examples.condition: If the 'oppositional' value, when used by a downstream character writer, consistently produces Uncs who read as satirized rather than inhabited — the perpetual contrarian who the narrative holds at arm's length, the IDW-coded Unc who serves as a target of the player's recognition rather than a subject they can inhabit — then the value violates the dignity rule at the craft level even if its description is nominally neutral. ZA/UM's test: can you write a compelling internal monologue from inside the 'oppositional' Unc's worldview that feels as real and coherent as an internal monologue from inside 'true-believer'? If not, the value is a satirical type, not a character substrate.
severity_examples.scenario: 'oppositional' cannot be written as a Disco Elysium haunting — it only reads as satirical commentary

severity_examples.condition: If a playtester shown 'vocationally-absorbed' and 'traditionally-loyal' cannot recognize the types-of-guy these values are meant to generate — if the vocabulary is too abstract to trigger the recognition response — then the abstraction move from culture-coded (NPR-liberal, talk-radio-conservative) to posture-coded (gradualist, true-believer) has broken the game's core pleasure mechanic. The brief states: 'the game's central pleasure is recognition. Politics values must be recognizable as types-of-guy, not abstract taxonomic buckets.' This is a P1 if the posture vocabulary is too opaque to trigger recognition without the culture-coded cross-product.
severity_examples.scenario: The abstract posture vocabulary loses recognition-hooks the game's central pleasure depends on

severity_examples.condition: If the 'gradualist' characterization produces Uncs who are described as balanced and reasonable but whose internal monologue is empty — they have no specific relationship to political events, no characteristic way of reading political news, no behavioral-under-stress signature — then the value is a surface type rather than a character substrate. The Disco Elysium/CK3 craft standard: every value should produce a character who has a distinctive *relationship to political events* that shapes his vocabulary and behavior, not just a characteristic *opinion about politics*.
severity_examples.scenario: 'gradualist' generates a surface (reasonable, moderate, institutional) without an interior (specific embodied relationship to political events)

success_hints: The internal-monologue test for each value: write 2-3 sentences in the character's voice that show his political substrate without stating a position. 'Traditionally-loyal' might think about the road-paving project in terms of who promised it and who delivered, not in terms of party ideology. 'Vocationally-absorbed' might not think about politics at all except when the union contract comes up or his permit gets delayed. 'Oppositional' might notice the contradiction in every official statement before engaging with its content. Values that cannot pass this test are position-coded rather than substrate-grounded.

The ZA/UM respect test for each value: could ZA/UM's writing team render this political substrate as a haunting — a genuine way of being in the world with explanatory power and failure modes — rather than as a satirical type? Values that can only be written satirically have failed the dignity rule at the craft level.

Cross-product recovery test for the v0 sketch: for each of the 7 original values, specify exactly which combination of draft-posture × class × region × media-era generates the same recognition-hook. If the combination is too complex to be reliable (requires 4+ specific values to align), the draft has lost a recognition-hook that needs to be recovered as a modifier or a 9th value.
task_context: Reviewing the 8-value politics-coding draft for Unc Rancher's procedural character generator through a procedural narrative and game-design craft lens — assessing whether each value is substrate-grounded enough to generate politically-inflected characterization without position-coding or mockery, applying Disco Elysium's haunting-model and Crusader Kings III's behavioral-signature model as craft standards, and evaluating whether the abstraction move from culture-coded to posture-coded values preserves or destroys the recognition-hooks the game depends on.
